topic: distributed systems; Byzantine consensus; communication topology
status: source-supported model tradeoff; broader empirical generality unverified
claim: The 2012 generalized-fault IABC result characterizes feasibility by an exact reduced-graph source-component condition under its synchronous directed-network model. A 2021 Relay-IABC paper changes the communication primitive—signed multi-hop relaying—and uses that stronger/more expensive information flow to claim convergence under sparser/local communication. Its simulation suggests faster convergence in one random-graph setup, but does not establish that end-to-end performance improves once flooding and cryptographic costs are counted.

sources.title: Iterative Approximate Byzantine Consensus under a Generalized Fault Model
locators: §5, Algorithm 1: locally feasible fault sets and trimming

sources.title: An Analysis of Multi-hop Iterative Approximate Byzantine Consensus with Local Communication
locators: §§III–V: signed multi-hop Relay-IABC model and convergence

interpretation: This is a bounded comparison of two primary papers, not a claim of global novelty. Relay-IABC changes the communication assumptions rather than falsifying the 2012 theorem. The reported faster convergence is based on a narrowly specified simulation and excludes a complete cost comparison for flooding/signature verification.
falsifiable_question: Under matched synchrony, Byzantine budgets, and termination error, does signed Relay-IABC reduce end-to-end latency on sparse networks after counting messages, bytes, signature-verification work, and failures across graph diameters, adversarial strategies, and random seeds? Identify the density/diameter regime where communication savings or convergence gains outweigh relay overhead.
primary_outcome: Rounds and wall-clock time to a fixed honest-state error threshold, total messages/bytes, signature verifications, energy, and failure probability under matched graph/fault scenarios.
counterevidence_and_caveats: The 2012 theorem is limited to its stated synchronous directed-network and fault-domain model.
The 2021 simulation uses one Erdos-Renyi setting with 30 honest and 14 Byzantine nodes; uncertainty across seeds is not reported in the reviewed section.
The 2021 paper explicitly notes flooding is communication-heavy.
Different papers use different communication primitives and convergence accounting; their headline iteration rates are not directly interchangeable.
Venue status for the 2021 arXiv version was not independently verified.
suggested_design: Implement both protocols behind a shared simulator and reproduce each paper's setup first. Then preregister a factorial sweep over graph density/diameter, node count, Byzantine strategies, and at least 30 graph/adversary seeds. Match final error and synchrony assumptions; log rounds, wall-clock, message/byte volume, signature checks, and energy separately.
